controls.title: HTTPS-only mode
controls.summary: Every http:// page load is upgraded to https://. If the upgrade fails, a warning page offers one Continue to site button, and the exception is kept per site and listed in settings. localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and *.localhost load over http with no warning page.
default_set_in: patches/hardening/0001-default-https-only-mode.patch: the default of the https_only_mode_enabled pref in chrome/browser/ui/browser_ui_prefs.cc

patches/hardening/0007-full-https-only-warning-page.patch: kHttpsFirstDialogUi is off by default in components/security_interstitials/core/features.cc, so the failed upgrade shows the warning page and not a native dialog
controls.cost: Sites and devices that only speak http (router and NAS admin pages, printers, old intranet apps, captive portals) show a warning page first. The exception is one click and lasts 15 days from the last visit.

options.label: Balanced (warn only for sites that usually use HTTPS)

controls.title: Third-party cookies
controls.summary: Cookies set or sent by a site embedded in another site are blocked.
controls.cost: Cross-site single sign-on that relies on cookies, embedded payment or login widgets and some video embeds can fail. Site exceptions and the Storage Access API are the escape hatches.

options.label: Allow third-party cookies (blocked in Incognito only)

controls.title: Partitioned storage
controls.summary: Storage used by an embedded site (localStorage, IndexedDB, caches) is kept separate for each top-level site.
default_set_in: Chromium: net/base/features.cc, kThirdPartyStoragePartitioning is enabled by default
controls.cost: An embedded widget no longer shares its state between sites, so it can ask the user to sign in again on each site.

controls.title: WebRTC IP leak protection
controls.summary: WebRTC only uses the default public network interface, so a page cannot read the local network addresses of the device.
default_set_in: patches/hardening/0005-allow-webrtc-policy-in-settings.patch: lets the settings page read and write the pref (Aerie adds the row)
controls.cost: Some video calls and peer-to-peer apps cannot find a direct path and fall back to a relay, which adds delay. Stricter values can break calls that have no relay.

controls.title: No prefetch or preloading
controls.summary: Speculative loads are off: link prefetch, prerender, preconnect, DNS prefetch and speculation rules. rel=preload and modulepreload are ordinary page loads and are not touched.
notes: Data Saver and Battery Saver also turn link prefetch and renderer DNS prefetch off, even when the setting is not Off (the check runs IsSomePreloadingEnabled with should_ignore_saver_modes=false).
A change of the setting reaches open tabs only when their WebPreferences are next recomputed (reload or restart).
controls.cost: Page loads are slightly slower, because the browser no longer opens connections or fetches pages ahead of a click.

controls.title: Strict site isolation
controls.summary: Every site gets its own renderer process, so a compromised page cannot read another site in memory.
default_set_in: Chromium: chrome/common/chrome_features.cc, kSitePerProcess is enabled by default on desktop
controls.cost: Uses more memory, because each site runs in its own process.

controls.title: JavaScript JIT per site
controls.summary: The JavaScript optimizing JIT (TurboFan and Maglev) is on for speed. Turn it off for a single site in Site settings, JavaScript optimization. A site with the JIT off never shares a process with a site that has it on.
default_set_in: Chromium: components/content_settings/core/browser/content_settings_registry.cc, the javascript-optimizer content setting is registered with CONTENT_SETTING_ALLOW as its default

helium-chromium/patches/ungoogled-chromium/move-js-optimizer-unfamiliar-sites.patch: registers the unfamiliar sites pref (default off) in content settings now that the Safe Browsing prefs are gone, so the setting page loads and the default stays allow
upstream: chrome/browser/chrome_content_browser_client.cc (AreV8OptimizationsEnabledForSite, SiteIsolationPolicy hook that isolates a site with an exception)
content/browser/site_info.cc (are_v8_optimizations_disabled is part of the SiteInfo)
content/browser/renderer_host/render_process_host_impl.cc (IsSuitableHost refuses to reuse a process with a different optimizer mode, and the renderer starts with --disable-optimizing-compilers)
notes: The setting is the upstream javascript-optimizer content setting, so it also shows in the site details page and in Settings, Privacy and security, Site settings, Additional content settings. It applies on the next visit to the site in a new tab, or after a restart. An embedded frame, or a page opened from another tab, keeps its current process until you open the site in a new tab, because upstream only swaps the process on a main-frame navigation in a tab with no related windows. An exception for a non-default port (for example `http://host:8080`) does not apply, because the site URL has no port, so the rule is the same for every port of the host. It is kept in the profile across restarts.

Process rule: the optimizer mode is part of the SiteInfo and of the renderer process flags. IsSuitableHost returns false for a process whose mode differs, so a site with the JIT off is only ever given a process that was started without the optimizing compilers, and a site with the JIT on is never given that process.
controls.cost: Pages that run heavy scripts, such as web apps, games and large spreadsheets, can run several times slower on a site with the JIT off. Turn it off only for sites you do not trust.

controls.title: Fingerprinting protection
controls.summary: Canvas and audio output and the reported number of CPU cores carry small random noise. The noise differs for each site and for each browser session, and is the same on every address of one site (www.example.com and shop.example.com share it). A private window starts with its own noise. You can turn it off for a single site, and that covers every address of the site. WebGL reports only the vendor family of the graphics card (for example Google Inc. (AMD)), and WebGPU reports no adapter details. The reported device memory is capped at 8 GB, and the cap stays when this is turned off.
default_set_in: helium-chromium/patches/helium/core/noise/canvas.patch and audio.patch: the canvas and audio noise
patches/hardening/0010-mask-the-gpu-in-webgl-and-webgpu.patch: the kHeliumNoiseWebGL feature is on by default
notes: Audio noise is seeded from the site and session only, so one site gets the same audio output on every render and every AnalyserNode read of the same signal in one session. A tracker cannot average the noise away by reading again.

The noise is keyed on the site: the scheme plus the registrable domain (the public suffix list decides which part that is). Every address of one site gets the same canvas, audio and core count, so a tracker cannot tell the addresses apart by their noise, and the per-site switch is one pattern, https://[*.]example.com, for the same addresses. The scheme is part of the site, so http://example.com and https://example.com have separate noise and separate switches. Older per-address off settings are widened to the site the first time the setting is read or changed. The key function leaves room for a second component, so keying on the Workspace later is a small change.

The seeds are created from random numbers when a browser context first asks for noise tokens and are held as data of that browser context (Helium's HeliumNoiseTokenData in content/browser/helium_noise/noise_token_data.cc, from base::RandUint64() in its constructor); that code writes no seed to disk. Only per-site values derived from a seed reach web pages, never the seed itself. A private window has its own seeds, different from the normal profile's and from every earlier private window. A per-site off setting made in a private window is kept in memory only, is gone when the window closes, and never applies to the normal profile (unit tests in components/aerie_fingerprint).

Device memory (navigator.deviceMemory, in workers, and the Device-Memory and Sec-CH-Device-Memory headers) is capped at 8 GB, where Chromium's desktop maximum is 32 GB. A machine with less than 8 GB keeps its real bucket. There is no noise on this value. The cap is the one exception to the rule that turning fingerprinting protection off restores the real value: it follows the HeliumNoise feature only, so it stays on when the setting is off, globally or for one site, and only --disable-features=HeliumNoise lifts it.

WebGL vendor and renderer (WEBGL_debug_renderer_info) report the vendor family in Chrome's own format, for example Google Inc. (AMD) and ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon Graphics, OpenGL ES 3.2). The families are AMD, Intel, NVIDIA and Mesa (llvmpipe); a card that matches none of them reports Intel, because Chrome never reports an other family and Intel is the most common one on Linux. The model, driver and LLVM version are dropped. Other WebGL parameters and extension lists are not changed. A site that picks graphics quality from the card model gets the generic family instead.
WebGPU adapter info has an empty vendor, architecture, device and description. Aerie's own code does the family mapping and the masked strings (components/aerie_gpu_info), with unit tests.

The WebGL and WebGPU values follow the same switches as the other noise: the browser sends the page a token only when protection is on for the site, and turning it off for the site or for the whole browser gives the real values back. A worker has no token yet, so it always gets the masked values until workers get tokens (issue #113); a worker started from a site with protection off therefore still sees masked values. The chrome://flags entry that sets a fixed WebGL value (SpoofWebGLInfo) still wins over the masking when you set it.
controls.cost: Sites that hash a canvas for bot defense can show more CAPTCHAs, and canvas editors that compare pixels can misbehave. Turn it off for a single site in the fingerprinting page. Turning it off does not lift the 8 GB device memory cap.

controls.title: Widevine DRM
controls.summary: Widevine decodes protected video and audio (Netflix, Disney+ and similar). It is a component made by Google. Aerie builds it in but neither downloads nor loads it until you turn this on, and Aerie sends nothing else to Google, and nothing at all about it until you turn it on. The first time a site asks for protected content, Aerie asks once whether to turn it on. After the download Aerie needs a restart to finish turning it on.
default_set_in: overlay/components/aerie_widevine/widevine_opt_in.cc: aerie.widevine.enabled is registered in Local State with default false
patches/widevine/0001-register-widevine-only-when-opted-in.patch: the Widevine component is registered with the component updater only once the pref is true
controls.cost: Turning it on downloads a closed-source Google module, which is checked against a pinned signing key before it loads, and lets Aerie ask Google for updates to it. Until you do, DRM video does not play. Before this setting, the CRLSet (the list of revoked certificates) got updates only while Widevine was on; now Aerie never sends the CRLSet to Google, so it is not updated.

controls.title: Extensions cannot loosen these settings
controls.summary: An extension with the privacy permission cannot write the WebRTC policy, the preloading option or the third-party cookie setting. Only the user can change them, in settings. Reading them and being told about changes still works.
default_set_in: patches/hardening/0006-lock-hardened-prefs-from-extensions.patch: the write permission of three chrome.privacy entries is removed in chrome/browser/extensions/pref_mapping.cc
controls.cost: Privacy extensions that set these options through chrome.privacy get a permission error. The user can still make the same change in settings.

manual_test.intro: The fingerprint run is manual and outside the Bench, because the Bench sends no traffic to outside sites and these test sites are outside it. Run it by hand after a slice that changes a fingerprint surface, and write the result in the Result column below with the build train and the total in bits.
procedure: Use a build that has the change, with a profile that has Fingerprinting protection on (the default) and no per-site exception for the test sites.
Open Cover Your Tracks (coveryourtracks.eff.org) and run the test. Write down the total in bits and the bits of each surface in the table.

Open browserleaks.com and read the WebGL, WebGPU, Canvas, Fonts and JavaScript pages (JavaScript shows the screen, the device memory and the number of cores). Write down what each one reports for the surfaces in the table.
Repeat step 2 once with Fingerprinting protection turned off for the site, to see the real values. Turn it back on after.
The baseline run had NextDNS on. That changes the tracker blocking half of Cover Your Tracks and not the fingerprint half, so say in the Result column if NextDNS or another DNS filter was on.

baseline.label: build train 8 (maintainer, 2026-11-08), Cover Your Tracks result strong protection, fingerprint randomized

rows.value: ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon RX 6600 (radeonsi navi23 LLVM 20.1.2), OpenGL ES 3.2)

deferred.title: Workers
deferred.reason: A worker gets no noise token yet (issue #113), so a worker always sees the masked WebGL values, also when protection is off for its site.

deferred.title: WebGPU adapter info
deferred.reason: Only the vendor, architecture, device, description and driver strings are emptied. The adapter limits, the feature list and the subgroup sizes are real values.

deferred.title: Device memory above 8 GB
deferred.reason: The baseline showed 32 GB because upstream raised the desktop maximum from 8 to 32 GB (crbug.com/454354290). Aerie caps it at 8 GB, and that cap stays when protection is off, so a site never learns the real value.

deferred.title: Client rects noise
deferred.reason: getClientRects and getBoundingClientRect noise exists upstream but is off and uses a per-document factor. Left to a follow-up issue.

deferred.title: measureText noise
deferred.reason: Canvas measureText noise exists upstream but is off and uses a per-document factor. Left to a follow-up issue.

deferred.title: WebGL fingerprinting noise
deferred.reason: WebGL readback and vendor strings are not covered by Helium noise. This is the largest item and a compatibility risk. Left to a follow-up issue.
